hook: An FBI-submitted monochrome still image captured by a U.S. government sensor system showing an unidentified dark, irregular object near the center of a crosshair reticle, with faint swirling background patterns and redactions applied prior to AARO submission.
why_it_matters: This image represents a rare instance of the FBI formally submitting UAP imagery to AARO under the post-2022 disclosure framework, indicating the Bureau has active sensor systems producing UAP-relevant data. The absence of an accompanying mission report and the withholding of date and location data limits analytical value, but the FBI's formal reporting chain to AARO is itself significant. The operator's inability to positively identify the object meets the threshold for official UAP classification.
key_findings: The image was captured by a U.S. government system and submitted by the FBI to AARO — establishing an active FBI-to-AARO reporting pathway for UAP events.
Date and location of the event were deliberately withheld from the submission, preventing basic geospatial or temporal correlation with other known UAP reports.
The original imagery was altered with redactions before submission to AARO, meaning AARO itself received a degraded version of the source data.
No accompanying mission report was provided, stripping context about the operational circumstances, sensor type, altitude, and observing platform.
The object appears small, dark, and irregular in shape, positioned just below and right of the optical or sensor reticle center — consistent with a briefly acquired, unresolved target.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This image was formally submitted by the FBI to AARO as part of the congressionally mandated UAP reporting process, placing it directly within AARO's collection and resolution mandate.

The withholding of date, location, and mission context — and redactions applied before AARO submission — is consistent with interagency data-sharing constraints typical when intelligence community equities are involved.
